targets.authors: Cevoli, B., Watkins, C., & Rastle, K.
targets.title: What is semantic diversity and why does it facilitate visual word recognition?
targets.outcome_computational_quote: We are able to replicate this correlation using the data uploaded to OSF by Cevoli et al.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Finally, and most importantly, we replicated Cevoli et al.’s analyses of the relationship between semantic diversity and lexical ambiguity. Cevoli et al. found that ambiguity did not predict C20_SemD and argued that semantic diversity is unrelated to variation in a word’s meaning. H13_SemD, conversely, reliably covaried with polysemy in every stimulus set, though it was not related to homonymy.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original shared data and code are reanalysed. Authors explicitly reproduce the original correlation, while alternative vector scaling and covariates challenge the original no-polysemy conclusion. Original numbers are not declared discrepant.

reasoning: The central retested paper is Cevoli et al.; the original semantic-diversity work is earlier in the chain. Lexicon projects and ambiguity studies supply data or stimuli rather than separate retested behavioral findings. Foltz supplies the rationale for a vector-quality validation. Full article includes references and matches title and all authors.
